html:
SMTO-EML-0003 — SMTO won't send your email sign-in over an unprotected link

GUID: 1971566f-7753-56a8-a198-2ae372c438a7
Slug: email-gateway-transport-insecure
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • Your email account's sign-in details may only travel over an encrypted, verified connection, and one of the connections SMTO would use isn't protected. SMTO stopped before sending your sign-in or any email.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and look at the Gateway you use. If it shows Insecure legacy or Identity changed instead of Secure, ask the person who manages it to restore its secure connection. SMTO only hands email sign-in details to a Gateway whose identity it has verified over an encrypted link.
  2. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu, select your email sender profile, choose Reveal & edit value, and check that the tls mode is starttls or implicit_tls, not plain. Then select Save. The plain mode sends without encryption, which SMTO never allows together with a password or account sign-in.
  3. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the email connection for that sender profile. The test signs in without sending any email, so you can confirm the fix safely.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Secure, and the connection test reports the mail server is ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Gateways and email settings. Don't switch the profile to plain or turn off certificate checks to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Credential-bearing email or OAuth work was refused because the Controller-to-Gateway transport is not verified, the sender profile pairs tls.mode plain with authentication, or SMTP authentication was attempted without an active TLS channel.

What this means

  • Credential-bearing email/OAuth lacks verified Gateway transport, or authenticated SMTP is configured or observed without an active encrypted channel. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Credential-bearing email/OAuth lacks verified Gateway transport, or authenticated SMTP is configured or observed without an active encrypted channel.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish Controller-to-Gateway transport readiness from Gateway-to-SMTP TLS configuration.

How to fix it

  • If gateway_transport_ready is false, restore the Gateway's verified TLS identity so its badge in Settings › Setup › Gateways shows Secure (not Insecure legacy or Identity changed). In the email_smtp profile set tls.mode to starttls or implicit_tls whenever auth.type is password or oauth2; an SMTP 538 reply means the server requires encryption for that AUTH mechanism.
  • Use verified encrypted Gateway transport and SMTP STARTTLS or implicit TLS for password and OAuth authentication.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • Both relevant credential transport boundaries satisfy their verified encryption requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
